title: Algorithmic Primitives of Theory of Mind Benchmarks
abstract: arXiv:2604.17819v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Do Theory of Mind (ToM) benchmarks really test theory of mind, or are they actually testing parsing and algorithmic state tracking? While benchmarks vary modality and dialogue length, this paper finds that they re-encode the same few state transition algorithms. We create PDDL-Mind, a neuro-symbolic approach that recovers such algorithms and upstream inductive biases of ToM benchmarks explicitly by parsing narratives into the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) and executes candidate actions against a predefined set of update algorithms. Doing so provides program-verified state traces to the model. We use our method's performance gain to audit how much of a benchmark's difficulty our inductive bias absorbs. Across MMToM, MuMA, and FanToM, outsourcing parsing to programs alone brings performance close to strong agentic pipelines, while outsourcing state tracking to PDDL moves GPT-4o to close-to-human performance. translated_title: 心智理论基准测试的算法原语
translated_abstract: 心智理论（ToM）基准测试真的在测试心智理论，还是实际上在测试解析和算法化状态跟踪？尽管各基准在模态和对话长度上有所差异，本文发现它们其实重新编码了相同的少数几种状态转移算法。我们提出了PDDL-Mind，一种神经符号方法，通过将叙事解析为规划领域定义语言（PDDL），并针对一组预定义的更新算法执行候选动作，从而显式地恢复这些算法以及ToM基准测试的上游归纳偏置。这样做能够为模型提供经程序验证的状态轨迹。我们利用该方法带来的性能提升来审计我们的归纳偏置究竟吸收了多少基准测试的难度。在MMToM、MuMA和FanToM三个基准上，仅将解析任务外包给程序就能使性能接近强大的智能体流水线，而将状态跟踪外包给PDDL则使GPT-4o的性能提升至接近人类水平。我们展示了……
tldr: 该论文提出神经符号方法PDDL-Mind，通过将叙事解析为PDDL并由程序执行状态更新，揭示了主流心智理论基准实际上主要在测试解析和状态跟踪等算法能力而非真正的心智理论，并借此将GPT-4o的性能提升至接近人类水平。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes PDDL-Mind, a neuro-symbolic method that parses narratives into PDDL and executes program-verified state updates, revealing that Theory of Mind benchmarks largely test parsing and state-tracking algorithms rather than genuine ToM, and boosting GPT-4o to near-human performance.
